items.detail:
Declaring `owned` moves the Desk onto pulse/lib/publish.mjs's declared branch, which at :527 refuses on ANY uncommitted file under `content/` that the run did not declare — `commitBlocked = 'foreign-content'`, and :573 then returns `{published:false}` without pushing. This is correct and is exactly what the brief asked for, but it is a NEW outcome for the Desk: before this change a Desk publish with a stray dirty `content/` file swept it into the commit and pushed anyway. From now on a fully gated, merged, approved job can end with nothing reaching the live site because an unrelated agent left one entry dirty, and the only trace is one `commit` step line in the run log. MEASURED, not inferred: the same tree returns `{"published":false,"reason":"foreign-content"}` when `owned` is declared and `would run: git add data content` (i.e. would have published the stranger's draft) when it is not. Nothing in this diff is wrong — it fails in the safe direction, which is the direction the brief asked for. What is missing is an issue recording that the Desk's publish can now be blocked by a file no job in the run touched, so the first time it happens it is a known condition and not a fresh diagnosis.

The added paragraph says "The two 200s in that blockquote differ from each other and from the table row's 375,916 for the ordinary reason: the response is not byte-stable", but the measurement offered in support is four fetches inside one second spanning 376,057-376,065 — a ~50-byte band. Every 200 measured for this URL on 2026-09-04, across this job, the j-20260904-49 record and my own re-fetch, falls in 376,020-376,069; the table row's 375,916 sits ~104 bytes below that entire band and is the one count the cited measurement does not cover. The paragraph's conclusion ("a byte count here dates a fetch; it never identifies a document") is unaffected and correct, but the causal attribution of the 375,916 gap is an inference presented as a measured result. Either scope the sentence to the two blockquote counts and say the table row's larger gap is unexplained but equally not evidence of a change, or measure the drift across hours rather than seconds.

The evidence file's header says the raw transcript is a "node fetch+strip+count script, 2026-09-03; the huggingface.co/meta-models org page was fetched twice because its activity feed renders intermittently". Grepping "^=== https" over data/reviews/evidence/verify-meta-spark-weights-pending-status.raw.txt returns 11 fetch blocks and huggingface.co/meta-models appears exactly once (line 22). The underlying observation is real — that page's stripped length was 2556 in the transcript and 2548 when I fetched it myself minutes later — but as written the sentence describes a second fetch the transcript does not contain. Either capture both fetches, or say it plainly ("the page was fetched in both this run and the earlier one and rendered differently; only this run's is captured"). This is the same narrative-outruns-transcript shape the previous pass flagged, at much smaller scale, which is why it is carried rather than blocked on.
